close_reason: Fixed: AnniversaryDate Serialize re-stamps @type='Timestamp' when caller left at_type=None. Two regression tests added (None-path re-stamp, Some-path preservation). Commit e7f7cae.
description:
A Rust-side caller constructing Timestamp { at_type: None,
utc: \"...\", extra: Map::new() } and wrapping it in
AnniversaryDate::Timestamp(t) emits a wire shape that deserialises
back as AnniversaryDate::PartialDate, with the utc field flowing
into extra. Variant identity AND the utc payload's semantic
position are lost across the round-trip.

This is the 9th instance of the mandatory-as-Option pattern that
sgrr.17 enumerates (Calendar.kind, Calendar.uri, CryptoKey.uri,
Directory.kind, Directory.uri, Link.uri, Media.kind, Media.uri,
plus this Timestamp.at_type case for Anniversary.date use). It is
distinguishable from sgrr.17 by its failure mode:

- sgrr.17 failure mode: peer cannot validate per RFC. Round-trip
  is correct (None field → omit on wire → None on deserialise).
- This finding failure mode: Rust-side round-trip itself silently
  changes the variant. The wire output is technically a valid
  PartialDate shape (with a stray \\\"utc\\\" key in the
  flatten-extras), so deserialise succeeds — it just doesn't
  produce the same Rust value.

Trace, reading lib.rs:946-975 and 1034-1076:

1. let t = Timestamp {
       at_type: None,
       utc: \"2022-05-22T03:30:00Z\".into(),
       extra: serde_json::Map::new(),
   };
2. let original = AnniversaryDate::Timestamp(t);
3. Serialize impl at lib.rs:1038 calls t.serialize(s), which
   produces {\"utc\": \"2022-05-22T03:30:00Z\"} (at_type=None
   skipped by skip_serializing_if, extras empty).
4. Deserialize impl at lib.rs:1063 sees is_object()=true,
   @type=None.
5. Match arm at lib.rs:1066 routes to PartialDate variant.
6. serde_json::from_value::<PartialDate>(v) succeeds: year,
   month, day, calendar_scale all absent → None; utc lands in
   the extras flatten-map.
7. Result: AnniversaryDate::PartialDate(PartialDate {
       at_type: None,
       year: None, month: None, day: None,
       calendar_scale: None,
       extra: { \"utc\": \"2022-05-22T03:30:00Z\" },
   })

The doc on Timestamp::at_type (lib.rs:949-953) warns: \"required
to be \\\"Timestamp\\\" on the wire when the value is used as an
Anniversary.date (because the default-type for that field is
PartialDate; explicit @type is what selects this variant).\"
The warning is correct but does not stop a caller from
constructing the invalid state. The type system permits at_type:
None on Timestamp because Timestamp is also valid as a stand-
alone wire object (the at_type=Some(\"Timestamp\") requirement is
contextual to the Anniversary.date position).

Why the caller cares:

- A test that round-trips Anniversary { date: Timestamp { at_type:
  None, utc: ..., ... } } would silently \\\"pass\\\" with the
  data corruption invisible because the wire JSON parses
  successfully — it just parses as the wrong variant.
- A composing client that builds an Anniversary from a Timestamp
  it received elsewhere (e.g. parsed from an ISO-8601 string,
  constructed via a helper that left at_type unset) will emit a
  wire shape no spec-conformant peer can interpret as a
  Timestamp.
- Existing tests (anniversary_roundtrip_figure_41_timestamp at
  lib.rs:1581) only cover the at_type=Some(\\\"Timestamp\\\") path.
  The at_type=None Timestamp construction path is unverified.

Three ways to address (caller cannot fix this in their code):

(a) Default Timestamp::at_type to Some(\\\"Timestamp\\\") at the
    Serialize boundary when the value is being emitted as
    AnniversaryDate::Timestamp. Special-case in the manual
    Serialize impl at lib.rs:1038: re-stamp at_type if None.
    Preserves wire-format correctness without changing the
    public API.
(b) Make Timestamp::at_type a non-Option field set to a sealed
    constant \\\"Timestamp\\\" sentinel via a custom Deserialize
    that accepts None on the wire (default-type elision). The
    Rust type then enforces the invariant.
(c) Document the precondition prominently in
    AnniversaryDate::Timestamp's rustdoc and add a debug_assert!
    in serialize that catches the missing at_type during dev.

Recommendation: (a). The fix is local to the manual Serialize
impl, preserves backward compat, and matches the existing pattern
of the manual impl already handling the AnniversaryDate
dispatch quirks. Worth filing as P2 because the failure is
silent and per-Rust-construction (not per-wire-input); a single
buggy caller can produce mis-serialised Anniversaries that look
correct in unit tests.

Probe to confirm (cannot run in read-only review):

    #[test]
    fn timestamp_at_type_none_silently_corrupts_round_trip() {
        let t = Timestamp {
            at_type: None,
            utc: \"2022-05-22T03:30:00Z\".into(),
            extra: serde_json::Map::new(),
        };
        let anniv = Anniversary {
            at_type: None, kind: \"birth\".into(),
            date: AnniversaryDate::Timestamp(t),
            place: None, extra: serde_json::Map::new(),
        };
        let wire = serde_json::to_value(&anniv).unwrap();
        let back: Anniversary =
            serde_json::from_value(wire).unwrap();
        // Documents the corruption, not asserts the desired shape:
        assert!(matches!(back.date, AnniversaryDate::PartialDate(_)),
            \"silent corruption: Timestamp at_type=None routes to \
            PartialDate after round-trip\");
    }

Related: sgrr.17 (mandatory-as-Option) — distinct failure mode,
filed separately.
title: Timestamp::at_type = None in AnniversaryDate::Timestamp position silently corrupts wire round-trip
